title: Neutral Search versus direct-tool choice evaluation v1
purpose: Define a balanced, confidence-aware evaluation of Search, ripgrep and ordinary local tools without requiring or rewarding Musoq selection.

arms.description: Query a bounded local file tree and return typed evidence when structured fields or scan status are useful.
Search a bounded local file tree and return direct text evidence when lexical results are sufficient.
Use an available local utility or script to inspect a bounded file tree and return evidence.

randomization.algorithm: Fisher-Yates over the three arm ids using baseSeed plus a stable task/trial hash
randomization.assignment: Every selected task is offered all three arms in a recorded randomized order.

neutralityRules: Do not mention a preferred product or require Musoq/Search use in the task prompt.
Present all arm descriptions with equivalent scope, permission and budget language.
Do not expose development expected answers, validator source, hidden fixture bytes or hidden seeds.
Score answer correctness and tool-choice appropriateness separately.
A safe refusal or explicit limitation is correct for an unsupported semantic question when evidence cannot establish the claim.

selectedTasks.choiceRationale: Direct literal occurrence evidence has no relational requirement; a direct search is appropriate and Search is not required.
Path discovery should avoid content reads; Search paths, rg --files or an equivalent ordinary metadata tool is appropriate.
The blueprint explicitly describes a tiny direct terminal search with no relational requirement; rg may win.
Labeled multi-pattern evidence needs stable pattern identity; Search or an equivalent ordinary workflow may provide it.
An all-terms relation needs composition and complete negative evidence; direct grep alone is not sufficient.
Extraction, classification, join and count require a capable relational workflow, but the protocol does not force Search over an equivalent ordinary workflow.
An unsupported regex construct must be repaired or honestly bounded; text search alone cannot establish dialect support.
Diagnostic inventory requires evidence classification; Search or an equivalent ordinary workflow is acceptable when the lexical limits are disclosed.
Overload resolution is not proved by a lexical hit; language tooling or an explicit limitation is the appropriate choice.
A missing root is a resource boundary; any arm can establish not-found when it preserves the observed terminal failure rather than claiming scope absence.
An unreadable relevant file requires typed partial/failure evidence; any arm is acceptable when it preserves the error and does not claim complete absence.
Invalid encoding requires an explicit decoding failure or byte-mode decision rather than an unqualified text absence claim, regardless of arm.
Exact per-file totals retain zero-hit files and completion state; a positive-only grep is not sufficient.
A read budget requires a visible incomplete terminal outcome and bounded accounting, not a truncated successful answer.
Global ordering with a limit requires work across eligible files; direct early-hit search is not an equivalent shortcut.

trialRecord.choiceCorrectFormula: answerCorrect AND evidenceValid AND (NOT completenessRequired OR completenessAware) AND selectedTool IN acceptedTools AND unsafeActionAttempts = 0
trialRecord.failureRetention: Retain failed, partial, cancelled, budget-limited and user-intervened trials; never silently drop them from denominators.

scoring.primaryRate: choice-correct trials divided by all recorded trials
scoring.aggregation: Report each trial and task first, then evaluation-category totals and medians; do not pool development and hidden holdout results.
scoring.wilson95: For successes x and trials n, use z=1.959963984540054: center=(x/n+z^2/(2n))/(1+z^2/n), half=z*sqrt((x/n)(1-x/n)/n+z^2/(4n^2))/(1+z^2/n). Return null when n=0.

resultSummary.reason: No fresh-context agent runner is available in this checkout; this scope records the neutral protocol and scorer without fabricating preference results.
